REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and upheld to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for that woman. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so that they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community. Protection and empowerment of women and children currently become the focus in development. Between women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not made into a unit. In that context, in the regions related to women and children, regional regulations must be present regarding: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority. II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1Sufficiently clear

Article2Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration. Article3Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wound or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and or causes death. Letterb What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. Letter c What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. Letterd What is meant by intimidation is an act of ordering or prohibiting by threatening or shackling to harm so that the victim is unable to make choices for his or her best interests. Letter e What is meant by forced eviction is an act of commanding by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right that a person has to a place that is appropriate for him or her. Letterf What is meant by deprivation of liberty is an act of eliminating the right to be able to live based on the best interests of a person. Letterg What is meant by neglect is:

a. actions that result in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social; b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should; c. actions that neglect people within the scope of their household, even though according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. Letterh What is meant by "exploitation" includes:

a. actions that economically or sexually exploit children with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; b. actions with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain profit both material and immaterial. c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to gain profit, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Child victims of violence whose parental custody rights are revoked, their education becomes the responsibility of the Regional Government or foster parents who obtain custody rights from a court decision.

is positioned as an independent institution.

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and upheld to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for that woman. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so that they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community. Protection and empowerment of women and children currently become the focus in development. Between women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not made into a unit. In that context, in the regions related to women and children, regional regulations must be present regarding: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. Letter c What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. Letterd What is meant by intimidation is an act of ordering or prohibiting by threatening or shackling to harm so that the victim is unable to make choices for his or her best interests. Letter e What is meant by forced eviction is an act of commanding by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right that a person has to a place that is appropriate for him or her. a. actions that result in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social; b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should; c. actions that neglect people within the scope of their household, even though according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as to provide basic and specific service needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience. 12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of human rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.

20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and upheld to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for that woman. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so that they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community. Protection and empowerment of women and children currently become the focus in development. Between women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not made into a unit. In that context, in the regions related to women and children, regional regulations must be present regarding: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority. II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase participation of women and children in their social interactions.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of human rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER IX GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 19

(1)The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of regional protection and empowerment of women and children.

(2)The community is authorized to actively supervise the implementation of regional protection and empowerment of women and children.

(3)The authority of the community as referred to in paragraph (2) includes:

a. providing input; b. submitting questions and obtaining answers from responsible regional government officials;
c. requesting realization and concrete activities from those assigned duties and authority;
d. other matters that are constructive and provide solutions.

CHAPTER V SERVICES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government provides services to women and children victims of acts of violence and neglect.

(2) Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:

a. complaints; b. health rehabilitation;
c. social rehabilitation; d. social reintegration; and e. legal assistance and accompaniment.

CHAPTER X REGIONAL ACTION PLAN

Article 20

(1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.

(2) The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is manifested in the joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and to eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and human trafficking.

Article 16

(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business community for support in organizing protection for women and children in the Regional area.

(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:

a. information and opening of employment opportunities; b. provision of education and job training; c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence; and d. provision of capital assistance for independent enterprises.

Article 10

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and upheld to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for that woman. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so that they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community. Protection and empowerment of women and children currently become the focus in development. Between women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not made into a unit. In that context, in the regions related to women and children, regional regulations must be present regarding: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority. II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article3Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wound or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and or causes death. Letterb What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. Letter c What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. Letterd What is meant by intimidation is an act of ordering or prohibiting by threatening or shackling to harm so that the victim is unable to make choices for his or her best interests. Letter e What is meant by forced eviction is an act of commanding by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right that a person has to a place that is appropriate for him or her. Letterf What is meant by deprivation of liberty is an act of eliminating the right to be able to live based on the best interests of a person. Letterg What is meant by neglect is:

a. actions that result in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social; b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should; c. actions that neglect people within the scope of their household, even though according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. Letterh What is meant by "exploitation" includes:

a. actions that economically or sexually exploit children with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; b. actions with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain profit both material and immaterial. c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to gain profit, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

(2) Child victims of acts of violence who are placed in safe houses are provided with care according to their needs.

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and upheld to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for that woman. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so that they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community. Protection and empowerment of women and children currently become the focus in development. Between women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not made into a unit. In that context, in the regions related to women and children, regional regulations must be present regarding: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority. II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Letter c What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. Letter e What is meant by forced eviction is an act of commanding by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right that a person has to a place that is appropriate for him or her. Letter e What is meant by forced eviction is an act of commanding by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right that a person has to a place that is appropriate for him or her. Letterf What is meant by deprivation of liberty is an act of eliminating the right to be able to live based on the best interests of a person. Letterg What is meant by neglect is:

a. actions that result in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social; b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should; c. actions that neglect people within the scope of their household, even though according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. Letterh What is meant by "exploitation" includes:

a. actions that economically or sexually exploit children with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; b. actions with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain profit both material and immaterial. c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to gain profit, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Article 16

(1) The Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children establishes partnerships with the business community for support in organizing protection for women and children in the Regional area.

(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:

a. information and opening of employment opportunities; b. provision of education and job training; c. provision of educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence; and d. provision of capital assistance for independent enterprises.

What is meant by "trafficking in persons" is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether done within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. SUPPLEMENT TO THE REGIONAL GAZETTE OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 117

Article 11

(1) The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A)

has the authority to organize the protection of women and children. (2) The duty of the Regional Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) is to carry out protection of women and children in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 17

The Regent as the person responsible for the protection and empowerment of regional women and children has the authority to make changes to the management or dismissal of members if the existing management or members do not carry out their roles and functions.

CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

(1) Protection of women and children from acts of violence shall be conducted based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; and c. protection of victims.

(2) Protection of women and children from acts of violence aims to protect, respect, guarantee the human rights of women and children, and pursue the best interests of women and children.

Article 12

The membership of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) consists of elements of relevant agencies, vertical agencies, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, researchers, academicians and religious, customary, community leaders and activists for the protection of women and children in the region.

Article 7

(1) Women and children victims of acts of violence are placed in safe houses or places whose whereabouts are kept confidential and receive basic fulfillment in accordance with their rights.

(2) Child victims of acts of violence who are placed in safe houses are provided with care according to their needs.
